solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Water-raising device has somehow broken with end bit fallen off

indicators.note: an end bit falling off means the final letter of the preceding word is dropped
somehow says the letters arrive by some unstated route, so the word before it is jumbled

parts.note: the three letters of has, rearranged
duff is slang for broken or useless; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A pump for lifting water has broken down, with a part dropping off its end.
explanation.walkthrough: SHA plus DUF(F) gives SHADUF. 'Duff' is British slang for broken or useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaduf is the counterweighted pole and bucket used in Egypt and the Middle East to lift water for irrigation.

clue.text: Like chunk of cake to get rid of B&B sneaked in

indicators.note: letters sneaked in are slipped inside the other word

parts.note: to slay is to kill, getting rid of someone
the two letters B

explanation.surface: A guesthouse owner wants rid of a slab of cake smuggled into the bed and breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Slabby means thick and flat like a slab, which is how a chunky piece of cake is cut.

clue.text: Smelly animal revealed by three leading characters

wordplay.note: the first three letters of the alphabet run from A to C

explanation.surface: A stinking creature exposed by a trio of ringleaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people in a story; it means letters, and the first three of the alphabet are A TO C.
explanation.definitionFit: The atoc is a South American skunk, notorious for the foul spray it uses in defence.

clue.text: Carboniferous insect Indian's excited about

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is wrapped around the other
excited letters are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: the ant is an insect
the letters of Indian, rearranged

explanation.surface: An Indian person gets excited about a prehistoric insect.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is'. 'Carboniferous' looks like an adjective for the insect, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dinantian is the earliest epoch of the Carboniferous period in Europe, named after Dinant in Belgium.

clue.text: Accumulation of waste products in river to end floating up

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

indicators.note: in a down clue, floating up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an aim is an end or goal

explanation.surface: Waste piling up in a river, with rubbish rising to the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Uremia (uraemia) is a build-up in the blood of waste normally removed by the kidneys.

clue.text: Sweetheart's foot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a playful term of endearment
second meaning: a nursery word for a foot

explanation.surface: Someone's beloved's little foot, as if in a love poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', joining two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tootsy (or tootsie) is both an affectionate name for a darling and a childish word for a foot or toe.

clue.text: Such African people led astray could be seen in wasteland

indicators.note: things gone astray have wandered from their places, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Members of an African people who were led off course are spotted in a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: TSWANA plus LED, jumbled, gives WASTELAND. So take LED out of WASTELAND and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tswana are a Bantu people of southern Africa, the main group in Botswana.

clue.text: Pointless old piece of neckwear worn by seaman

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: what is worn goes around its wearer, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a tie is worn round the neck
OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor sports a useless old tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose means serving no useful purpose, so it is superfluous or futile.

clue.text: Historian understood the likes of you and me

parts.note: tacit means understood without being said

parts.words: the likes of you and me
parts.note: you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A historian who understood ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was the Roman writer whose Annals and Histories are a main source for the early Roman Empire.

clue.text: One mechanism set up in country for old native

indicators.note: the reversed pair is placed in the following word

parts.note: a state is a country

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the pair is turned to read upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a rig is apparatus or a mechanism

explanation.surface: Some device erected in the countryside for an elderly local.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stagirite is Aristotle, born at Stagira in ancient Macedonia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stagirite is a native of the ancient Greek town of Stagira, the title chiefly given to Aristotle.

clue.text: Desires being elevated in Disneyland

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated letters are read from bottom to top
in signals the letters sit inside the next word

parts.note: the middle run of this word

explanation.surface: Longings that are lifted while at a theme park.
explanation.definitionFit: Yens are cravings or yearnings, as in having a yen for travel.

clue.text: Like bird with broad bill and wiggly tail, sort to gain speed

indicators.note: something wiggly twists about, so the letters of the following words are jumbled
the jumbled words gain, that is take on, a further piece added at the end

parts.note: the eight letters of these two words, rearranged
rate as in speed of travel

explanation.surface: A description of a bird with a broad beak and a waggling tail that needs to speed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Latirostrate is a zoological term meaning broad-billed, from Latin latus (broad) and rostrum (beak).

clue.text: A character had briefly made reparation

indicators.note: briefly says the phrase is to be shortened to its contracted written form

parts.note: taken as written
tone is character or quality, as in the tone of a place
had contracts to 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: A person with a certain character had, in short, made amends.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make amends for a wrong, so the past tense matches made reparation.

clue.text: Peruvian person jailed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a member of the ancient empire of Peru
second meaning, split in two: in the can, can being slang for prison

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Peruvian has been locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the split reading IN CAN; 'the can' is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Incan describes a person of the Inca people, rulers of Peru before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Bend when admitting one sin — ordeal for murderer?

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the first word holds the others inside it

parts.note: a bight is a bend in a coast or rope
I is the Roman numeral one
to err is to sin

explanation.surface: A sinner bends and confesses under trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an old superstition rather than a standard sense of ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: The bier-right was a medieval test in which a suspect touched the victim's corpse; bleeding wounds were taken as proof of guilt.

clue.text: Tree visible in Assam landscape?

indicators.note: what is visible in a phrase can be seen inside its run of letters

parts.note: runs across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A tree one might spot in the scenery of Assam, the Indian tea state.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the tree really is Indian, so the surface is true as well as cryptic.
explanation.definitionFit: The amla is the Indian gooseberry tree, whose sour fruit is used in Indian cooking and medicine.

clue.text: Tufted species to grow wild

indicators.note: growing wild means running out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: all nine letters of both words

explanation.surface: A plant variety with tufts that spreads untamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cespitose (caespitose) is a botanical term for growing in dense clumps or tussocks.

clue.text: Somehow artificial bishop having a certain Greek style

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the Ionic order is a style of Greek architecture

explanation.surface: A bishop with a manufactured taste for Greek columns.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word is not an anagram signal; it qualifies the definition, since a bionic body is only partly artificial.
explanation.definitionFit: Bionic describes a body or limb enhanced with electronic or mechanical parts, so made artificial in some way.

clue.text: Begin to run ashore

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to start and take hold, as winter sets in
second meaning: of a tide or current, to flow towards the land

explanation.surface: Start to drive a boat onto the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to start and become established and, of the sea or wind, to move in towards the shore.

clue.text: Squire joining a king, fighter with little hesitation

parts.note: taken as written
R stands for Rex, Latin for king
a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A squire teams up with a king and a warrior who hardly hesitates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' suggests a soldier beside the squire; it is a jet plane.
explanation.definitionFit: An armiger is someone entitled to bear a coat of arms, a rank once held by an esquire.

clue.text: A repeated curse could make one pause for breath

indicators.note: could make says the preceding letters can be made into something new

parts.note: the letter A, given twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: Swearing over and over could make someone stop to catch their breath.
explanation.definitionFit: A caesura is a break or pause in the middle of a line of verse, often where a reader takes breath.

clue.text: Wedding not begun — old-fashioned Scottish service

indicators.note: a word not begun is missing its opening letter

parts.note: marriage, without its first letter

explanation.surface: A wedding that never got under way, in an old Scottish church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests a church ceremony to go with the wedding; here it is labour owed to a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriage was a feudal duty in Scotland: labour with horses and carts owed by a tenant to the landlord.

clue.text: Cattle joint — ring to enter

indicators.note: one piece is made to enter, going inside the other

parts.note: the ankle is a joint
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Cattle at a market, a joint of beef, and a ring to go into.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankole are a long-horned breed of cattle from East Africa, named after a region of Uganda.

clue.text: Shy bird turning up in spring

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to shy is to throw, and to lob is to throw
mag is short for magpie

explanation.surface: A timid bird appears in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' wants to be timid; here it is a verb, to throw. 'Spring' looks like the season but is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To gambol is to leap or skip about playfully, which is what a spring is.

clue.text: Daughter given a kick upset? Shame!

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written
to boot is to kick

explanation.surface: A daughter who was kicked is distressed, and that is a pity.
explanation.definitionFit: Too bad is an exclamation of regret, the same as saying what a pity.

clue.text: Fondness often dreaded, putting some outsiders off

indicators.note: removing some outer letters from each end leaves a run from inside the phrase

parts.note: the phrase less its first two and last four letters

explanation.surface: Affection is often feared, and puts some outsiders off.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendre is a fondness or soft spot for someone, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Primitive fellow in pine forest

parts.note: ur- is the German-derived prefix for original or primitive
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A caveman living among the pines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primitive fellow' reads as one idea, a caveman, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Urman is the name for the marshy coniferous forest of Siberia, a taiga of pine, spruce and fir.

clue.text: Nip toe badly, getting this ballet technique wrong?

indicators.note: badly done things are out of order, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: the six letters of both words

explanation.surface: A dancer pinches a toe painfully by doing a ballet move wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the technique done wrong: a jumble of 'nip toe' fits the pun, since dancing on the tips of the toes badly is just how a toe gets hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointe is dancing on the tips of the toes in blocked shoes, a core technique of classical ballet, here done wrongly.

clue.text: Temples with serving women once

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
the ATS, Auxiliary Territorial Service, was the British women's army of the Second World War

explanation.surface: Temples staffed by women servers in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A wat is a Buddhist temple or monastery in Thailand, Cambodia or Laos.

clue.text: Pithy saying — nothing to include in that discussion

indicators.note: one word is made to include, or hold within it, the other

parts.note: a mot is a witty remark, as in bon mot
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A short witty remark adds nothing to the debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot was a meeting or assembly for debate, and the word survives as a discussion or argument, as in moot court.

clue.text: Light touch preceding a final word

parts.note: a tat is a light tap or touch
taken as written

explanation.surface: A delicate finishing touch before the closing words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is an informal British goodbye, the last thing said on parting.

clue.text: Irritation produced by nameless gang or criminal

indicators.note: nameless means without N, the abbreviation for name
something criminal is crooked, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: gang with its N for name taken away
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trouble caused by an anonymous gang or a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for name. Aggro is British slang, short for aggravation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is informal British slang for aggravation: annoyance, hassle or aggressive trouble.

clue.text: Set up for travel in foreign parts right towards the end

indicators.note: the letter is shifted towards the end, so it is placed later in the word

parts.note: overseas
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a trip abroad, with things right at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the R out of ABROAD and put it back two places later: ABOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aboard is to be on a ship, train or plane, settled in for the journey.

clue.text: This man may be met with hoot, great Anselm being cracked up?

definitions.text: This man may be met with hoot, great Anselm being cracked up?

indicators.note: this man means the answer is the word man taken out of the following letters
something cracked up is broken into pieces and reassembled

parts.note: all fifteen letters of the three words, less M, A and N

explanation.surface: A shallow theologian gets hooted at while great Saint Anselm is praised to the skies.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumble HOOT GREAT ANSELM and this man is what is left after MAN is taken away. 'Cracked up' also means highly praised, the honour Anselm gets that the answer does not.
explanation.definitionFit: A theologaster is a shallow or petty theologian, the sort of pseudo-scholar who deserves derision rather than respect.

clue.text: Saunter as Irishman in street, then stagger

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
to reel is to stagger

explanation.surface: An Irishman strolls down the road, then lurches about.
explanation.definitionFit: Streel is an Irish dialect verb meaning to wander or trail about aimlessly.

clue.text: Imagine fish have to be caught

indicators.note: something caught is held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish
to have a meal is to eat

explanation.surface: Dreaming of having a fish to catch.
explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form an idea of something in the mind, a formal synonym of picture or conceive.
